title: One thread per slot
description:
Write `std::vector<int> squaresInParallel(int count)`.

It starts `count` threads. Thread number `i` (counting from 0) computes `i * i` and stores it in element `i` of a result vector. When all the threads have finished, the function returns the vector.

Use `std::jthread`, which joins automatically when it is destroyed. Keep the threads in a `std::vector<std::jthread>` inside an inner scope `{ }`; at that scope's closing brace every thread is joined, and only then is it safe to return the results.

Each thread writes to a **different** element, so no locking is needed.
hints: Capture `i` **by value** in the lambda. By the time a thread runs, the loop has moved on and a reference to `i` would see a different number.
